statements.impact_statement: Everything in the image already runs as root, so a setuid or setgid file extracted by tar grants nothing new. GNU tar only unpacks archives MadGraph wrote itself during a run; MadGraph's model, tool and PDF-set downloads go through wget, which the image doesn't include, and LHAPDF's own downloader uses Python's tarfile.
The attack needs physical fault injection on the CPU (modified supply voltage), which OpenSSL's security policy places outside its threat model.

The image runs no network services and no program in it passes input from elsewhere to this code. The glob() resource use needs an attacker-chosen pattern, such as an FTP server passing remote STAT arguments to glob().
File::Temp calls _is_safe only with safe_level MEDIUM or HIGH, and no Perl code in the image sets safe_level (checked /opt, including MadGraph's merge scripts).
The symlink race is in systemd-tmpfiles, which the image doesn't include; libsystemd0 and libudev1 are libraries only.

The memory exhaustion is in the ARM/HP template demangler (arm_pt, demangle_arm_hp_template, per the backtrace in sourceware bug 22009). libiberty's old-style demangler in cplus-dem.c (GNU v2, Lucid, ARM, HP and EDG schemes) was removed for GCC 9 in 2018 and from binutils since 2.32. The image's c++filt offers only none, auto, gnu-v3, java, gnat, dlang and rust, and rejects -s gnu, lucid, arm, hp and edg as unknown styles.
The race needs root to run chown or chgrp with -R -L on a tree another user can write to. The image has no other users and nothing in it runs chown or chgrp -R -L.

The overflow is in demangle_template, part of the old-style demangler. libiberty's old-style demangler in cplus-dem.c (GNU v2, Lucid, ARM, HP and EDG schemes) was removed for GCC 9 in 2018 and from binutils since 2.32. The image's c++filt offers only none, auto, gnu-v3, java, gnat, dlang and rust, and rejects -s gnu, lucid, arm, hp and edg as unknown styles. Siddhesh Poyarekar (GCC bug 88783) found it fixed from 2.32 on.

The over-read in d_expression_1 needs a crafted mangled name. Nick Clifton (binutils) reports the testcases no longer fail from 2.35 on (GCC bug 88629). In this image demangling happens only in ld's diagnostics, on symbols gcc and gfortran have just compiled from MadGraph's generated code, and in ROOT's crash handler, which can run addr2line and c++filt on the crashing process's own libraries (the image has no gdb). Neither sees mangled names from elsewhere.

statements.action_statement: http.client accepts a Content-Length with underscores or a sign ("1_0", "+10"), so a malicious server can desynchronise responses. In this image Python's HTTP client runs when MadGraph fetches its online model list or a URL given at a card prompt, when its update command is run (automatic checks are off), and when LHAPDF downloads a missing PDF set, all but the card URL from plain-HTTP servers. Provide models and PDF sets locally, for example in the mounted working directory, instead of letting MadGraph or LHAPDF download them.

The overflow (sourceware PR 34442) needs a malformed ELF object linked with --gc-sections -w. In this image ld only links objects that gcc and gfortran compile in the container from MadGraph's generated code, plus libraries the image ships, and MadGraph runs the linked programs right afterwards, so anyone who could put a crafted object in front of ld already controls code that runs.

Python's pyexpat module (in libpython-3.13-minimal) doesn't use the image's libexpat1: it is built with CPython 3.13.18's bundled expat 2.9.0, which lacks this fix. MadGraph parses only XML it wrote itself during the run (Pythia's DJR output, its results summary and histogram files).
